newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares to track Wall Street rise and fall.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares to track Wall Street rise and fall.

text.p: Firmer Belgian shares, which held in a narrow range on Wednesday, are expected to keep moving higher with interest rates still holding at low levels.
But a major sell-off in the United States could halt the market's progress, traders said. "We will keep heading higher unless Americans suddenly dump their shares," one said.

The Belgian bourse held up well on Wednesday compared with other European markets, even managing to close on a slightly positive note despite a lower Wall Street which sank back below the psychologically key level of 6,000 points in early business.
The Bel-20 share index .BFX ended the day 2.76 points or 0.15 percent up at 1,791.14, having traded in a 1,796.65/ 1,787.43 range. A total of 3.1 billion francs worth of Belgian shares changed hands.
Analysts note chart resistance at 1,800 points and support at 1,750.
However, traders noted the index was skewed on Wednesday by strong performances in a small handfull of heavily-weighted shares.
Cement maker CBR, oil major Petrofina and chemicals and drugs firm UCB rose sharply.
CBR is the subject of a number of buy recommendations on the basis of a predicted outperformance after the expiry between December 2 and 20 of a put warrant. It ended the day 35 francs up at 2,470.
Buy recommendations are out for Petrofina too on the basis of rising oil prices. It ended 1.6 percent up at 9,620.

After a share analysts' meeting on Tuesday UCB closed 1,300 francs higher at 64,400, having at one stage hit a record high of 64,900. Traders said it was undervalued by comparison with U.S. pharmaceutical stocks.
Dollar-sensitives also did well, traders noted.
They particularly pointed to retailer Delhaize which climbed 30 francs to 1,830, noting the firm's Food Lion unit in the U.S. had actually been a touch weaker on Tuesday.
